searchText: I definitely agree to adding that if we can find a place to put the list I mentioned above. No objection, but also no desire. I have argued in the past that the author line should be removed on final. 😄 I'll vote in favor of removing the author line when the EIPs get stuck into a cohesive document describing actual clients. Until then, I think knowing who to poke for more information is essential 😉 (Not that my vote counts for anything 🤣 ) Our Great Dictator might favourably consider your opinion though when making his unilateral decision 😉 No objection I have been thinking about a somewhat substantive change to EIP-3074, namely splitting it up into two opcodes, one for signature validation and one for the actual call. I wrote up the details here: https://ethereum-magicians.org/t/eip-3074-sponsored-transaction-precompile/4880/41?u=adietrichs I haven't personally verified it, but this seems to be a repository of all Etherscan-validated solidity sources on mainnet & ropsten: https://github.com/tintinweb/smart-contract-sanctuary https://github.com/tintinweb/smart-contract-sanctuary/blob/master/contracts/mainnet/c7/c7EE21406BB581e741FBb8B21f213188433D9f2F_VaultUSDT.sol#L978 That's interesting. `VaultUSDT` seems to have a blocklist for contracts that can be bypassed if `msg.sender == tx.origin`. do we know what kinds of contracts are usually greylisted? because if it is really only about "sender is EOA", then this is still true under 3074 I found other versions of this contract that use the openzeppelin `isContract` library function in that place instead https://github.com/OpenZeppelin/openzeppelin-contracts/blob/master/contracts/utils/Address.sol So the `isContract` pattern in general is probably relatively common. I think any version of programmable sponsored transactions breaks some assumptions there. Although invariants like "I can reliably send ETH to it without triggering any execution" of course still hold.
